sentences.text: BAIL APPL
CRIME NO.838/2024 OF Kuzhalmannam Police Station, Palakkad PETITIONERS:

1 AMSHAJ  AGED 30 YEARS  S/O HABEEB 15/610 AMSHU MANZIL KOYAMARAKKADU, PUDUSSERY  CENTRAL KANJICODE, PALAKKAD, KERALA, INDIA, PIN -  678621  2 SARA UMMA  AGED 75 YEARS  W/O ABDUL KAREEM THEMADATHIL VEEDU PARAVANI KUTHANUR  KUTHANNUR-I PALAKKAD KERALA, PIN - 678721  BY ADVS.
 RIZWANA A.A.
 AQIB SOHAIL P.S.
RESPONDENT:
 STATE OF KERALA  REPRESENTED BY PUBLIC PROSECUTOR,HIGH COURT OF KERALA,
 PIN - 682031  BY SR.PP - NOUSHAD K.A.
 THIS BAIL APPLICATION HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 10.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 BA No. 9526 of 2024 :2:
Amshaj vs State Of Kerala on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106395087/
1  2025:KER:10774  P.V.KUNHIKRISHNAN, J  --------------------------------
 B.A.No.9526 of 2024  -------------------------------
 Dated this the 10th day of February, 2025  ORDER
This Bail Application is filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
2. Petitioners are accused in Crime No.838/2024 of Kuzhalmannam Police Station.
Above case is registered against the petitioners alleging offence punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
Petitioners are accused Nos.1 and 5.
The 1st petitioner is the husband of the defacto complainant and the 2nd petitioner is the grandmother of the 1 st petitioner.

3. The prosecution case is that, the petitioners mentally and physically harassed the defacto complainant demanding additional dowry and asserting that 15 sovereigns of gold jewellery provided by her family as wedding gift were inadequate.
4. Heard counsel for the petitioners and the Public Prosecutor.
Admittedly, the offence alleged against the petitioners is a matrimonial offence.
It seems that the marital relationship between the 1st petitioner and the defacto complainant is in existence.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, and also considering the fact that matrimonial offence is alleged, I think the petitioners can be released on bail after imposing stringent conditions.
6. Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chidambaram.

P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870],
after considering all the earlier judgments, observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

entities.text: P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. Recently the Apex Court in Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
considered the point in detail.

entities.text: Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the above judgment is extracted hereunder.
"12. We may note that personal liberty is an important aspect of our constitutional mandate.

The occasion to arrest an 2025:KER:10774 accused during investigation arises when custodial investigation becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.

sentences.text: Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.
A distinction must be made between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.

(Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189:
(1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981))

entities.text:
Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189:
(1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person.

If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact, throughout cooperated with the investigation we fail to appreciate why there should be a compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused."

8. In Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961], the Apex Court observed that even if the allegation is one of grave economic offence, it is not a rule that bail should be denied in every case.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Considering the dictum laid down in the above decision and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Bail Application is allowed with the following directions:
2025:KER:10774 1.
The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.

2. After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the petitioners,
they shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) each with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer concerned.
3. The petitioners shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation as and when required.

The petitioners shall co- operate with the investigation and shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
4. Petitioners shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.
5. Petitioners shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which they are accused, or suspected, of the commission of which they are suspected.

3 6.

Needless to mention, it would be well within the powers of the investigating officer to investigate the matter and, if necessary, to effect recoveries on the information, if any, given by the petitioners even while the petitioners are on bail as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663].
7.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any of the above conditions are violated by the petitioners, the jurisdictional Court can cancel the bail in accordance to law, even though the bail is granted by this Court.
The prosecution and the victim are at 2025:KER:10774 liberty to approach the jurisdictional Court to cancel the bail, if any of the above conditions are violated.

Sd/-
P.V.KUNHIKRISHNAN, JUDGE sbk/-
